solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Surviving letter to the Corinthians that’s unknown within New Testament (6)

indicators.note: within means inside, so X is set inside ETA, splitting it after the E

blocks.note: a Greek letter, as the Corinthians would write

annotation.surface: A scholar notes which of Paul's letters to Corinth still survives in the New Testament.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface points at St Paul's epistles to Corinth; the 'letter' is a single character of the Greek alphabet the Corinthians wrote in.
annotation.definitionFit: Extant documents are those that have survived to the present.

clue.text: One of the horses departs after stock’s reduced (5)

indicators.note: D is placed after the shortened EQUIP
EQUIP is cut short, losing its last letter

blocks.note: EQUIP (stock, as a verb: to supply) minus its last letter
d = departs, as on a timetable

annotation.surface: A stable runs low on feed and one of its horses is sold off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stock' is a verb here: to stock a shop is to equip it.
annotation.definitionFit: An equid is any member of the horse family, so one of the horses.

clue.text: Seafarer with apostolic brief that may help him weather the storm (9)

definitions.text: that may help him weather the storm

indicators.note: TAR is joined with what follows
PAULINE is cut short, losing its last letter

blocks.note: PAULINE (of the apostle Paul) minus its last letter

annotation.surface: A sailor carries a short Pauline text to see him through a storm, as if prayer were his shelter.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests prayer as protection; the practical protection is a waterproof sheet. Tarpaulin was also old slang for a sailor, so the seafarer is doubly apt.
annotation.definitionFit: A tarpaulin is a waterproof sheet that keeps a sailor and his gear dry in a storm.

clue.text: Service vehicle pulled up on side of motorway (4)

indicators.note: in a down clue, pulling up reverses VAN
in a down clue, the reversed VAN sits on top of Y
the end side of motorway gives its last letter

annotation.surface: A service vehicle has pulled over on the hard shoulder of a motorway.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Service vehicle' reads as one phrase; split it, and Service is the armed service.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Senior Service is Britain's navy, one of the armed forces known collectively as the services.

clue.text: Cat chased by dogs, possibly very fast ones (8)

indicators.note: what is chased has its pursuers behind it, so WHIP comes first and PETS follow

blocks.note: the cat o' nine tails is a whip
dogs are an example of pets

annotation.surface: A cat is chased by dogs, some of which are very fast.
annotation.walkthrough: The cat is the cat o' nine tails, a whip; nothing feline about it. Whippets are the racing dogs the surface half-promises.
annotation.definitionFit: Whippets are slim racing dogs bred for speed.

clue.text: Husband may put up with pony for a term (e.g. pony as horse) (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting MAY up reverses it to YAM
PONY stands in place of A

blocks.note: PONY replaces the A in YAM, giving YPONYM

annotation.surface: A husband may tolerate a pony for a while, as the example tacked on the end plays along.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put up with' reads as tolerate; split it, and 'put up' reverses MAY while 'with pony for a' swaps PONY in for A.
annotation.definitionFit: A hyponym is a more specific term under a general one, as pony falls under horse.

clue.text: Pants erupt with smell [becoming] foul (10)

indicators.note: pants as an adjective means rubbish, so the letters of ERUPT are rearranged
the anagram is joined with SCENT

annotation.surface: A pair of trousers is let down by a foul smell.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like trousers, or a verb; it is the British slang adjective for rubbish, used here to signal an anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: something putrescent is decaying, and rotting matter is foul in smell and look.

clue.text: Inaccessible place for brooding heroine touring India (5)

indicators.note: EYRE goes round I, as a tourer goes round a country

blocks.note: India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: A moody heroine travels round India.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brooding' seems to describe the heroine's mood; it belongs to the definition, where birds brood their eggs.
annotation.definitionFit: An eyrie is an eagle's nest built high on a crag where the birds brood their young.

clue.text: Baseball infielder[’s] two items of clothing (9)

annotation.surface: A baseball player's kit is described in terms of what he wears.
annotation.walkthrough: The two garments simply sit side by side.
annotation.definitionFit: The shortstop fields between second and third base, an infield position.

clue.text: Heartlessly knock down powerless friend — no longer buddy? (6)

indicators.note: FLOOR loses its middle letter
PAL loses P, the abbreviation for power

blocks.note: FLOOR (knock down) without its central O

annotation.surface: Someone flattens a weakened friend and is no longer his buddy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Buddy' reads as mate, echoing 'friend'; here it means in bud, so something no longer in bud has come into flower.
annotation.definitionFit: A plant no longer in bud is in flower, and floral means of flowers.

clue.text: Take apart a French composer (7)

annotation.surface: A critic dissects a French composer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A French composer' reads as one phrase; the article is French too.
annotation.definitionFit: To unravel something is to pull it apart thread by thread.

clue.text: Small marsupial droppings collecting round hill (7)

indicators.note: POO collects TOR inside it

blocks.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor
a round letter, O, following the hill inside POO

annotation.surface: A naturalist identifies a small marsupial from its droppings near a hill.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Round hill' looks like one rounded hill; it is two pieces, O after TOR, both collected inside the droppings.
annotation.definitionFit: The potoroo is a small Australian marsupial related to the kangaroo.

clue.text: Take in room in hospital round (4)

indicators.note: to turn something round is to face it the other way, so WARD is read backwards

blocks.note: a ward is a hospital room

annotation.surface: A patient is taken into a hospital room on the doctor's round.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like a ward round; it is only the instruction to turn WARD back.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the breathing sense: you draw breath or take in air.

clue.text: Parisian is by mountains in Australia [in] colourful outer layer (6,4)

indicators.note: mountains in Australia puts the RANGE inside OZ, splitting it after the O
EST is placed beside the rest

annotation.surface: A Frenchman stands by the mountains of Australia.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Parisian' is the usual signal that a word is French. The surface never hints at fruit, which is what hides the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Orange zest is the brightly coloured outer layer of an orange's peel.

clue.text: Person orchestrating hypnotism set to start with suspect (10)

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters are not in their true order
only the first letter of set is taken

annotation.surface: Someone is setting up a hypnotism session, starting with a suspect under interrogation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Set to start with suspect' reads as a plan to begin with a suspect; the phrase actually breaks after 'with', so 'suspect' is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a symphonist writes symphonies, scoring the parts for a full orchestra.

clue.text: Better half of pop song a hit [in] language of SW India (9)

blocks.note: pop is father; his better half is mother, MA
a lay is a song or ballad
to lam is to hit hard

annotation.surface: A pop song half of which became a hit in India.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Better half of pop song' reads as the stronger half of a record; 'pop' is dad, and his better half is MA.
annotation.definitionFit: Malayalam is the Dravidian language of Kerala, in south-west India.

clue.text: Scots are unaware of packages Southern Post Office delivered in error (9)

indicators.note: MISKEN wraps round S and PO like a parcel

blocks.note: misken is Scots for fail to know or recognise

annotation.surface: Scottish recipients don't know about parcels the Post Office delivered to the wrong address.
annotation.walkthrough: Packages and the Post Office paint a misdelivery; 'delivered' is about speech, and 'packages' is the container signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Words misspoken were delivered in error, said wrongly.

clue.text: French oil producer [having] Renault’s front end checked by dipstick (5)

indicators.note: R is held in check inside COOT
the front end of Renault is its first letter

blocks.note: both are slang for a fool

annotation.surface: A French car's oil is checked with a dipstick.
annotation.walkthrough: Oil, Renault and dipstick all say car maintenance; the 'oil producer' is a painter in oils, and dipstick is slang for an idiot.
annotation.definitionFit: Jean-Baptiste-Camille Corot was a French landscape painter who worked in oils.

clue.text: The knowhow to drive land yacht? (9)

blocks.note: a road is the land route, as opposed to sea
a yacht is an example of a craft; the question mark flags the example

annotation.surface: Someone wonders what skill you would need to steer a yacht on land.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Land yacht' is a real sand vehicle, which makes the phrase look whole; the question mark says yacht is only one example of a craft.
annotation.definitionFit: Roadcraft is the skill and judgement of driving well on the road.

clue.text: First light turning ornamental cherry tree leaves red to begin with (5)

indicators.note: the tree's name is turned back to front
leaves is the verb, to depart, so R departs from the tree's name
only the first letter of red is taken

blocks.note: first letter of red, taken away

annotation.surface: At dawn the ornamental cherry turns and drops its first red leaves.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like foliage on the tree; it is a verb, telling R to go.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, mainly American: sunup is dawn, when the day's first light appears.

clue.text: Retired fireman working with a special buzzer on the wall? (5,4)

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so SAM is reversed

blocks.note: Fireman Sam, the children's TV character

annotation.surface: A retired fireman takes a job fitting a special alarm buzzer to a wall.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Buzzer on the wall' sounds like a doorbell or alarm; the buzzer is an insect, and the question mark flags the wordplay on its mud nest built on walls.
annotation.definitionFit: Mason wasps build nests of mud, often on walls, and buzz.

clue.text: Monsieur visiting his dear one who perhaps arranged their meeting (7)

blocks.note: M. is the French abbreviation for monsieur
at = visiting, as in at the Smiths'

annotation.surface: A Frenchman visits his sweetheart, and someone wonders who introduced them.
annotation.walkthrough: The French theme runs through: M and CHER are both French, for the Frenchman and his darling.
annotation.definitionFit: A matcher pairs people up, as a matchmaker might have arranged their meeting.

clue.text: Pomeranian dog quaffing river spray (6)

indicators.note: to quaff is to drink, and what the dog drinks ends up inside it, so R goes inside SPITZ

blocks.note: the Pomeranian is a type of spitz

annotation.surface: A little Pomeranian laps at a river and sprays water about.
annotation.walkthrough: The Pomeranian is one of the spitz family of dogs.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, from German spritzen: a spritz is a quick squirt or spray, of perfume or water.

clue.text: Possibly flyer’s getting new blue cape (10)

blocks.note: a flyer is one kind of promo, a promotional leaflet
blue is the colour of the Conservative (Tory) party in Britain

annotation.surface: An aviator is kitted out with a new blue cape.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' suggests an airman and 'cape' a garment; the flyer is a leaflet, and the cape is a headland.
annotation.definitionFit: A promontory is a headland jutting into the sea, as a cape does.

clue.text: Primate managed to intercede in self-inflicted blunder (5)

indicators.note: RAN steps in between the O and G

blocks.note: an own goal (OG) in football, a self-inflicted blunder
to run a business is to manage it

annotation.surface: A church leader steps in after someone's own blunder.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Primate' can mean an archbishop, which fits the interceding; here it is the ape.
annotation.definitionFit: The orang, short for orangutan, is a great ape, a primate.

clue.text: Leave hastily [from] self-catering apartment on vacation (4)

indicators.note: apartment is vacated, emptied of its middle

blocks.note: S/C is the abbreviation in holiday listings
first and last letters of apartment

annotation.surface: Holidaymakers flee a self-catering flat in a hurry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' reads as on holiday, which the self-catering flat encourages; it means emptied.
annotation.definitionFit: Scat is an order to go away quickly, so to leave hastily.

clue.text: One of several sharp nails left alongside fences (5)

indicators.note: the phrase fences the answer in, enclosing it

blocks.note: the letters run from the last of left into the start of alongside

annotation.surface: Some sharp nails are left lying beside a fence.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fences' looks like the noun, somewhere to leave nails; it is a verb meaning encloses.
annotation.definitionFit: A talon is one of the sharp claws of a bird of prey.

clue.text: Deride junior ingesting double dose of ecstasy (4)

indicators.note: to ingest is to swallow, so JR takes the EE down inside itself

annotation.surface: Someone mocks a youngster who took two ecstasy pills.
annotation.walkthrough: E is the standard drug-culture abbreviation for ecstasy.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to jeer is to mock someone loudly, a noisy way of deriding them.

clue.text: Bats vanish after entrance of knight errant (7)

indicators.note: the entrance of knight is its first letter
bats as an adjective means crazy, so the letters are scrambled
the anagram comes after K

annotation.surface: Bats disappear as a knight errant enters.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Knight errant' is a set phrase, but 'errant' is the definition on its own. Bats is the crazy adjective, not the animals.
annotation.definitionFit: Errant can mean straying from what is right, and knavish means dishonest.

clue.text: Elation about little piggy’s growth? (7)

indicators.note: the letters of elation are moved about

annotation.surface: Delight over a little pig putting on weight.
annotation.walkthrough: The little piggy is a toe, from the nursery rhyme 'This little piggy went to market' played on a child's toes.
annotation.definitionFit: A toenail grows on a toe, the little piggy of the rhyme.

clue.text: Worthless loco finally retired from sweet old railway (8)

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the last letter of loco is used
to retire is to withdraw, so that O withdraws from the sweet

blocks.note: last letter of loco, taken out of NOUGAT

annotation.surface: A worthless old locomotive is retired from a quaint heritage railway.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sweet old railway' reads as a charming heritage line; the sweet is nougat, which loses the O at the end of loco.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, from Latin nugae (trifles): a nugatory sum or effort is trifling and of no worth.

clue.text: British School [of] Language in Rennes (6)

blocks.note: Eton College, the English public school

annotation.surface: A British school teaches a language spoken in Rennes.
annotation.walkthrough: Rennes is the capital of Brittany, where Breton is spoken.
annotation.definitionFit: Breton is the Celtic language of Brittany, whose capital is Rennes.
